scenes.anchor_text: Frankly, Olive was a bit on the fence about this whole grad school thing. Not because she didn’t like science.  And not because of the truckload of obvious red flags. She was well aware that committing to years of unappreciated, underpaid eighty-hour workweeks might not be good for her mental health.
scenes.scene_description: A wide establishing shot of Stanford campus, hinting at the overwhelming nature of graduate studies Olive is contemplating.

scenes.anchor_text: Held her back, that is, until she was invited to interview for a spot in Stanford’s biology department, and came across The Guy. The Guy whose name she never really got. The Guy she met after stumbling blindly into the first bathroom she could find.

scenes.anchor_text: All she could see was a watery outline—someone tall, dark haired, dressed in black, and . . . yeah. That was it. “I . . . is this the ladies’ restroom?” she stammered.
scenes.scene_description: Olive's blurry perspective of the tall, dark-haired figure in the dimly lit bathroom, creating a sense of mystery and intrigue.

scenes.anchor_text: “We don’t use this as a restroom, just to dispose of waste and wash equipment.” “Oh, sorry. I thought . . .” Poorly. She’d thought poorly, as was her habit and curse.

scenes.anchor_text: Olive could smell a whiff of eugenol, and laundry detergent, and clean, male skin. An oddly nice combination.

scenes.anchor_text: The hand that closed around hers was dry, and warm, and so large it could have enveloped her whole fist. Everything about him must be huge. Height, fingers, voice.

scenes.anchor_text: Heavy thoughts to have in the presence of a stranger, in the darkness of her closed eyelids. So she cracked them open; her vision was still blurry, but the burning was mostly gone. The Guy was looking at her.

scenes.anchor_text: “It’s the best one.” He was smiling, she thought. Or something like it. “Good luck on your interview, Olive.” “Thanks.” He was almost out the door already.
